3,4-Alkadienyl Ketones via the Palladium-Catalyzed 
Decarboxylative Allenylation of 3-Oxocarboxylic acids 
Tonghao Zhu a and Shengming Ma a,b  
In this communication, we will report a palladium-c atalyzed 
decarboxylative allenylation of benzyl carbonates a nd tert -butyl 
carbonates of 2,3-allenol with 3-oxocarboxylic acid . The reaction 
provides a new and straightforward approach to 3,4- dienyl 
ketones under mild conditions. 
Allenes are particularly attractive building blocks  in organic 
synthesis because of their ability to undergo a var iety of 
transformations. 1 Thus, the development of efficient methods 
for the synthesis of functional allenes is of high interest. So far, 
the methods for the synthesis of allenones, especia lly 3,4-
dienyl ketones, have not been well established. In general, 
they are synthesized stepwise by α-allenylation of 1,3-
dicarbonyl compounds or imines with buta-2,3-dienyl  bromide 
followed by  corresponding decarbonylation or hydro lysis; 2 
SN2’-type substitution of α-imido lithium organocupra tes with 
diethyl buta-1,3-dien-2-yl phosphonate or 3-(1,3-di oxolan-2-
yl)-alkyl magnesium bromide  with  propargylic bromides 
followed by hydrolysis; 3 SN2 substitution of allenyllithium with 
4-(1,3-dioxolan-2-yl)-alkyl bromide and hydrolysis; 4 
dibromomethylation of the acetals of ω-alken-2-ones  treated 
with methyllithium or magnesium; 5 sequential 1,2-addition of 
carbon nucleophiles to β-carbonyl cyclohexenol triflates, C-C 
fragmentation and β- elimination.6 In addition, oxidation of the 
alka-4,5-dienols may produce the corresponding 3,4- allenyl 
ketones.4,7 All these methods suffer from multi-steps and not-
really-available starting materials. Thus, there is  an urgent 
demand for the development of a convenient and effi cient 
synthesis of 3,4-allenones under mild conditions fr om really 
available starting materials. 
Recently, much attention has been paid to the trans ition 
metal-catalyzed reaction of 2,3-allenyl compounds w ith 
leaving groups and nucleophiles, such as 1,3 -dicarbonyl 
compounds8 or amines, 8b,9 affording allenes with a nucleophilic 
functionality. Inspired by these previous works and  our 
interest on allene synthesis, we herein report a pa lladium-
catalyzed intermolecular decarboxylative allenylati on of 3-
oxocarboxylic acids 10  for the efficient synthesis of 3,4-
allenones under mild reaction conditions.

Our investigation began with the reaction of nona-1 ,2-
dien-4-yl acetate 1a  and 3-phenyl-3-oxopropanoic acid 2a . 
Initially, we optimized the reaction condition by s creening 
different ligands combined with Pd 2(dba) 3·CHCl 3 as catalyst 
and LiOBu t as base in THF at 25 oC (Table 1, Entries 1-8). We 
found that L8 was the best ligand of this reaction, which 
afforded the decarboxylated product  3aa  in 55% NMR yield 
(Table 1, Entry 8). The normal expected product 3aa’ was not 
detected in the crude reaction mixture. Although th e yield of 
3aa  with ligand L7 (54%, Table 1, Entry 7) was slightly lower 
than L8 , it was far cheaper, 11  so we chose L7  as the ligand for 
further optimization. Further screening of other pa lladium 
sources (Table 1, Entries 9-12), such as [Pd(π-cinn amyl)Cl] 2, 
[Pd(allyl)Cl] 2, Pd(OAc) 2 and Pd(PPh 3)4, showed that 
Pd 2(dba) 3·CHCl 3 is still the best.

the catalyst and 2.0 equiv. of LiOBu t as the base, subsequent

Further study was directed to the effect of leaving  group,

With the optimized conditions in hand, the scope of  this 
reaction has been investigated and the results are summarized 
in Table 4. When R 1 group is n-C5H11 or n-C6H13 and Ar is phenyl, 
the reaction afforded the corresponding products 3aa  and 3fa  
in 79% yields (Table 4, Entries 1 and 2); moreover, alkyl group 
R1 with many synthetically useful functional groups, such as 
OTHP, OBn, C=C bond and C-C triple bond may be 
accommodated (Table 4, Entries 6-9); R 
1 may be also aryl 
groups bearing halide, COOMe, CN ( 1m-r) generating the 
corresponding products in 44-62% yields (Table 4, En tries 10-
15). For the scope of Ar, synthetically attractive Br ( 2b ) or Cl 
(2c ) could be accommodated (Table 4, Entries 4 and 5), 
however, it is worth noting that the reaction shoul d be 
conducted at 50 oC; Ar may also be 2-thienyl group ( 2g) , 2-furyl 
group ( 2h) , or  2-naphthyl ( 2i). Furthermore, we could easily 
conduct the reaction of 2.2 g (7.5 mmol) of 1f to provide  1.26 g 
of 3fa  (Table 4, Entry 3). The reaction of tert -butyl dodeca-1,2-
dien-5-yn-4-yl carbonate 1s with  3-(naphthalen-2-yl)-3-
oxopropanoic acid 2i afforded the desired product 3si in 49% 
yield (Table 4, Entry 16).

To understand the mechanism of the reaction, we tri ed the 
reaction of benzyl deca-1,2-dien-4-yl carbonate 
1f  with 
acetophenone 4a  under standard conditions. It was found that 
no desired product 3fa  was formed (Scheme 2, Eq. 1). When 3-
oxocarboxylic acid 2a  was directly stirred in THF, 
acetophenone was generated in 5% NMR yield after 12  h 
(Scheme 2, Eq. 2a). However, in the presence of 
Pd 
2dba) 3·CHCl 3 and binap, acetophenone was generated in 83% 
NMR yield with no D-incorporation upon quenched wit h D 2O 
(Scheme 2, Eq. 2b). Finally, we found that the reac tion of 2a  
with LiOBu t alone afforded acetophenone- d3 in 62% yield and 
75% of D-incorportion upon quenching with D 2O (Scheme 2, Eq. 
2b). The reaction of acid 2d  with Pd 2(dba) 3·CHCl 3 and binap 
showed the similar results of 2a, however, its reaction with  
LiOBu t is much slower  (Scheme 2, Eq. 3a and 3b). 
Based the above results, a plausible mechanism is p roposed as 
shown in Scheme 3. A methyleneallylic palladium(II)  complex 
A12  was formed via the oxidative addition of 1 with the Pd(0) 
catalyst. Then, there are two possible pathways. Path A : The 
complex  A  undergoes the ligand exchange to form 
methyleneallylic palladium(II) 3-oxocarboxylate B. After the  
decarboxylation,  methyleneallylic palladium(II) enolate 
intermediate C is formed (see Eq. 2b and 3a). Path B : 
decarboxylation of 3-oxocarboxylic acid 2 occurs under 
existence of base to form the enolate 2’  first (see Eq. 2c and 
3b), which undergoes the subsequent ligand exchange  with 
complex A to form intermediate C. Reductive elimination 
would give the final product 3 and regenerate the Pd(0) 
catalyst to complete the catalytic cycle.

In conclusion, we have developed a palladium-cataly zed 
decarboxylative allenylation of benzyl carbonates o r tert -butyl 
carbonates of 2,3-allenols with 3-oxocarboxylic aci ds. The 
reaction provides a new, straightforward approach t o 3,4-
dienyl ketones under mild conditions. Due to the es aily 
availablity of both starting materials and the cata lyst as well as 
simple operation, this method will be useful in org anic
